ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
On the right side of a smooth horizontal platform, there exists an infinite uniform magnetic field with magnetic induction strength \( B \), directed perpendicularly outward from the plane of the paper. At the right end of the platform, there is a small ball \( Q \) with mass \( m \) and a negative charge \(-q\). On the left side, there is an insulating ball \( P \) with mass \( M = 4m \) and no charge, moving horizontally with an initial velocity \( v_{0} = \frac{m g}{q B} \) directly toward \( Q \) to the right, resulting in a head-on collision. During the collision, there is no mechanical energy loss, and no transfer of charge occurs. The height of the horizontal platform above the ground is \( h \), the gravitational acceleration is \( g \), and air resistance is negligible.

1. What are the velocities of the two balls, $P$ and $Q$, after an elastic head-on collision?
2. What is the horizontal distance $x$ from the landing point of ball $P$ after the collision to the right end of the platform?
3. After the collision, the charge of the small ball $Q$ remains unchanged. Under the influence of gravity and the magnetic force, what is the maximum height $H$ above the ground that the small ball $Q$ reaches after the collision? What is the velocity $v$ of the small ball $Q$ at that moment?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
$\frac{3m g}{5q B}$, $\frac{8m g}{5q B}$, both directions to the right
$\frac{3m}{5q B}\sqrt{2g h}$
$h + \frac{6m^{2}g}{5q^{2}B^{2}}$, $\frac{2m g}{5q B}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, a horizontal platform is located on the left side and is higher than the ground line below; small ball P is on the left side of the platform, with a velocity arrow v0 pointing to the right beside it; small ball Q is located near the edge of the right end of the platform. In the area on the right side of the platform, many dots are drawn and labeled B, indicating that the magnetic field is perpendicular to the plane of the paper outward; from the right end of the platform downward there is a vertical dashed line to the ground, and near the bottom it is labeled 0. According to the meaning of the problem, the height of the platform above the ground is h. Reasoning: Take horizontally rightward as +x, vertically upward as +y. Before the collision, the mass of P is 4m, its velocity is v0=mg/(qB), the mass of Q is m, and its initial velocity is 0. After the elastic head-on collision, by the one-dimensional elastic collision formula: vP'=(4m-m)/(4m+m) v0=3v0/5=3mg/(5qB), vQ'=2(4m)/(4m+m) v0=8v0/5=8mg/(5qB). Both are to the right. P is uncharged, and after the collision flies out from the right end of the platform with horizontal velocity vP'=3mg/(5qB), subject only to gravity. The falling time satisfies h=gt^2/2, so t=sqrt(2h/g). The horizontal distance x=vP't=(3mg/(5qB))sqrt(2h/g)=3m sqrt(2gh)/(5qB). Q carries negative charge -q, and after entering the magnetic field is subject to gravity and the Lorentz force. Let ω=qB/m, then the equations of motion are: dvx/dt=-ω vy, dvy/dt=ω vx-g. Let u=vx-g/ω, then u'=-ωvy, vy'=ωu. Initially vx(0)=8v0/5=8g/(5ω), vy(0)=0, so u(0)=8g/(5ω)-g/ω=3g/(5ω)=3v0/5. Thus u=(3v0/5)cos(ωt), vy=(3v0/5)sin(ωt), vx=v0+(3v0/5)cos(ωt). Q first rises, and when it reaches the highest point for the first time, vy=0, corresponding to t=π/ω. The increase in height Δy=∫0^{π/ω} (3v0/5)sin(ωt)dt=2(3v0/5)/ω=6g/(5ω^2)=6m^2 g/(5q^2B^2). Therefore the height of the highest point above the ground is H=h+6m^2g/(5q^2B^2). At this time vx=v0-(3v0/5)=2v0/5=2mg/(5qB), vy=0, so the speed magnitude is 2mg/(5qB), and the direction is to the right.
